children: Lithuania’s trade deficit narrowed to €223.3 million in August 2026 from €274.4 million in the same month last year, as exports grew faster than imports.

Exports increased by 14.9% year-on-year to €3,461.0 million, mainly driven by higher exports of mineral fuels, mineral oils and products of their distillation (41.2%), cereals (66.6%), and ground vehicles and parts thereof (27.1%).
Imports rose by 12.1% to €3,684.3 million, reflecting increased imports of mineral fuels, mineral oils and products of their distillation (26.4%), and ground vehicles and parts thereof (24.7%).
For the January-August period, Lithuania’s trade deficit narrowed slightly to €4,414.7 million from €4,422.7 million a year ago.
During this period, Lithuania’s goods were primarily exported to Latvia, which accounted for 13.4% of total exports, followed by Poland (11.9%) and Germany (9.0%).
Imports were sourced predominantly from Poland (12.2%), Germany (9.3%), Latvia (8.6%), and Netherlands (7.7%).

title: Lithuania Trade Deficit Narrows Slightly in August
